Sky Forge – Chapter 14: The Iron Choir

Posted on November 2, 2026 by translator

Previous Chapter | Table of Contents | Next Chapter

TL Note: this chapter was a monster to translate, enjoy!

The bells of the forge city did not ring; they sang. Every morning, four hundred iron throats opened above the smelting halls and filled the valley with a chord so low that the birds flew in circles until it was over.

Kael had heard it every day of his life, and every day it had meant the same thing: work. Today it meant something else. Today it meant the trial.

He climbed the long stair behind his sister, counting the steps the way their mother had taught them, one breath for every ten. At the top, the air was hot enough to taste.

“Do you remember the first verse?” Lysa asked without turning around.

“I remember all of them.”

“Good. Forget the third one. They changed it last winter.”

The choirmaster waited for them beside the great anvil, a thin woman with soot in the lines of her face and a tuning fork hanging from a chain around her neck. She did not smile. In twenty years, nobody in the city had seen her smile, and the apprentices liked to say that her face had been cast in a mould and cooled too quickly.

“Sing,” she said.

So he sang. The first note came out thin and uncertain, but the iron answered it, a deep hum rising from the anvil beneath his hands, and with every line the metal grew warmer until the whole platform shook with a sound that was half his voice and half the mountain’s.

Translator’s rant: the author uses the same word for “sing” and “forge”, which is a pun I could not keep.
